destination.name: Brewarrina
destination.tagline: A Barwon River town beside Baiame's Ngunnhu, stone fish traps that may be the oldest human construction in the world.
destination.description: Brewarrina is a small town of 1,651 people (2016) on the Barwon River in north-western New South Wales. The Aboriginal fish traps there, also called Baiame's Ngunnhu, are on the State Heritage Register and the National Heritage List, and may be the oldest human construction in the world. The Brewarrina Aboriginal Cultural Museum, opened in 1988, adjoins the site. The town lies on the lands of the Muruwari, Ngemba, Weilwan and Yualwarri peoples.
whyVisit: Walk beside Baiame's Ngunnhu fish traps
Learn at the Aboriginal Culture Museum
Join a guided Aboriginal cultural tour

goodToKnow.title: Tours start at the museum
goodToKnow.detail: Guided tours leave from the museum; Wikivoyage lists 20 dollars for adults, but times are unverified, so ask at the museum or visitor centre.

goodToKnow.title: Weekday hours
goodToKnow.detail: The museum is open Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and the visitor centre at 57 Bathurst Street, Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

goodToKnow.title: Hot summers
goodToKnow.detail: Summers are frequently over 40 degrees, so the cooler months are easier for walking the traps.
